selected_cases.name: production model configuration accepts public HTTP without a private-network override
production public HTTP reaches the configured model transport with authorization and the exact request body
public HTTP support retains private-network and metadata restrictions
actual worker request commits frozen attribution, dispatch and validated usage without recording private input or charging twice
terminal frames wait for durable usage and hand off to the next request without an asynchronous busy gap
the database rejects missing usage, inconsistent prices and unsuccessful HTTP outcomes without releasing a dispatched request
fractional per-request costs retain an exact numerator for one aggregate rounding without posting duplicate ledger charges
prepared rate promises serialize before any HTTP dispatch and cancellation returns only unused promises
new policy is enforced again at dispatch without silently applying an old permit's limits
revocation after admission is rechecked before fetch and retains known zero spend
cancellation after durable dispatch intent but before fetch is proven zero and releases both capacity and rate promise
unterminated response remains unknown and consumes actor capacity across a fresh runtime
an orphaned dispatch intent becomes unknown once and retains shared capacity without replay or zero-spend fabrication
expired prepared permits are reclaimed with immutable zero-spend events and cannot later dispatch
a completed provider request keeps its rolling-minute rate charge after freeing concurrency
one operation can never be replayed into another provider request even after a known cancellation
request and policy history cannot be rewritten and ordinary RLS cannot expose another actor's or tenant's request
four actual Node workers share the database admission ceiling across two tenants
exact counting includes the normalized context and binds one proof to the actual generation bytes
unverified or unpriced input counting makes zero provider calls and never guesses a token count
malformed exact count retains its platform commitment and blocks a new attempt without generation
text and image share one original reservation and an over-budget image is blocked before HTTP
concurrent requests serialize one task budget while task counting is funded only by the platform
input count mismatch preserves actual spend then blocks the next call and final settlement for reconciliation
output above its explicit bound is recorded as real usage and cannot widen the customer budget
the platform counting pool is shared across tasks and cannot draw from a customer wallet
one count proof cannot authorize a different generation hash or be consumed twice
unsupported context fields are rejected before counting rather than omitting part of a paid model input
